authorization: Carl, chat 2026-10-24: "Yes go ahead with the four requests, R1 to R4" (relayed by the coordinator); under his earlier ruling, rights-checked public archive files only. Terms were read before each download and are quoted below.

tessFfi.what: 84 consecutive TESS 200-second calibrated full-frame images (ffic) of camera 1, CCD 2, sector 56, 2022-09-04 04:15 to 08:52 UTC, around the transit of HD 209458 b at BTJD 2826.78; an 81 by 81 pixel cutout of each about HD 209458
tessFfi.source: https://stpubdata.s3.amazonaws.com/tess/public/ffi/s0056/2022/247/1-2/<name>_ffic.fits (STScI public dataset on AWS, which mirrors MAST; accepted as MAST by Carl, chat 2026-10-24)
tessFfi.readAs: two byte ranges per file: the headers (bytes 0 to 14,399) and 81 rows of the calibrated image (the cal extension starts at byte 14,400; rows of 2,136 big-endian float32 pixels, 8,544 bytes each): 692,064 bytes. 84 files, 59,342,976 bytes read in all; nothing else of the files was read.
tessFfi.terms: MAST data use policy (https://archive.stsci.edu/publishing/data-use, read 2026-10-24): "Most data hosted at MAST are in the public domain ... and therefore do not have restrictions on use"; the originating mission and STScI are to be acknowledged. TESS mission data have no proprietary period.
tessFfi.decision: admitted, public domain; the cutout is committed (2,204,496 bytes)

cutout.origin: zero-based array indices of the FFI image, so the first pixel of each frame is column 1130, row 316

tessFfi.units: electrons/s, calibrated (bias, dark, flat, smear, vignetting and dead time applied; BACKAPP false: the background is NOT subtracted), as the archive writes them
tessFfi.noSkyWcs: the FFI headers carry only a physical WCS (RAWX, RAWY) and no sky WCS
tessFfi.anchor: the frames are placed by the pack tess-hd209458-s56-frame: the zero-based pixel of the FFI array is that pack pixel plus (1165, 352), found by normalised cross-correlation of the pack frame (11 by 13) with the FFI stripe (0.998 at that offset, every flip and transpose lower: 0.987 at best), and the pack WCS carried to the cutout by adding (35, 36) to CRPIX. It is an anchor for matching stars, not a solution: the legs fit their own.
tessFfi.gainAndReadNoise: the TPF header values of the pack (gain 5.19, read noise 9.5496, CCD output D), as the pack uses them; the FFI header gives 5.11 and 7.358 (output C) for the columns the cutout lies in by the array coordinates. The two sources disagree on the output, which this record does not resolve; the effect on the bright stars is below the contract bounds.

gaia.what: Gaia DR3 sources of the field of HD 209458
gaia.query: SELECT Source, RA_ICRS, DE_ICRS, e_RA_ICRS, e_DE_ICRS, Plx, e_Plx, pmRA, pmDE, e_pmRA, e_pmDE, RUWE, Gmag, BPmag, RPmag FROM "I/355/gaiadr3" WHERE 1=CONTAINS(POINT('ICRS',RA_ICRS,DE_ICRS),CIRCLE('ICRS',330.7951,18.8842,0.3)) AND Gmag<17 ORDER BY Gmag

answer.file: not committed: the whole cone is kept out of the repository

subset.rule: rows of the answer whose pixel falls within 1.5 pixels of the cutout by the anchor WCS, with Gmag 16 or brighter

gaia.terms: ESA Gaia data licence (https://www.cosmos.esa.int/web/gaia-users/license, read 2026-10-24): "Gaia data are distributed under the CC BY-NC 3.0 IGO license." The ESA space science archives terms (https://www.cosmos.esa.int/web/esdc/terms-and-conditions, read 2026-10-24): data are "open and free to use ... subject to proper acknowledgment"; commercial use needs ESA authorisation. VizieR (https://cds.unistra.fr/vizier-org/licences_vizier.html): free for scientific use, cite the catalogue, the copyright follows the data origin.
gaia.decision: redistribution is allowed with credit and non-commercially, so it does not forbid committing; the repository already keeps one non-commercial Gaia fixture (LICENSES.md, NOTICE, OWNER_ACTIONS.md). Only the 222-row subset is committed, flagged non-commercial, with the credit line; the owner question of whether a non-commercial fixture belongs in an archive at all (OWNER_ACTIONS.md) now covers this file too.
gaia.credit: This work has made use of data from the European Space Agency (ESA) mission Gaia (https://www.cosmos.esa.int/gaia), processed by the Gaia Data Processing and Analysis Consortium (DPAC). Gaia Collaboration, Vallenari et al. (2023), A&A 674, A1.

hipparcos.what: the Hipparcos new reduction row of HD 209458 (HIP 108859)
hipparcos.source: CDS VizieR TAP, table I/311/hip2 (van Leeuwen 2007, A&A 474, 653)
hipparcos.terms: ESA space science archives terms (https://www.cosmos.esa.int/web/esdc/terms-and-conditions, read 2026-10-24): CC BY-NC 3.0 IGO, "open and free to use ... subject to proper acknowledgment". The ESA Hipparcos pages and the VizieR ReadMe of I/311 carry no separate licence text.
hipparcos.decision: one catalogue row, committed, flagged non-commercial with the credit line (van Leeuwen 2007; ESA Hipparcos)

jplSmallBodies.what: three JPL small-body identification answers for the field of HD 209458 at the start, middle and end of the frames (04:15:00, 06:33:00 and 08:52:00 UTC on 2022-09-04), V 19 or brighter, geocentric, a 0.6 degree square
jplSmallBodies.file: not in the repository: removed on Carl's ruling (chat 2026-10-24, "Go with your recommendation on each"); only this record is kept
jplSmallBodies.negativeSearch: no asteroid inside the 0.6 degree square about HD 209458 at any of the three times: every candidate is fainter than V 17.6 and more than 0.3 degree away; the nearest planet (Neptune) is 32.7 degrees away (astropy built-in ephemeris)
jplSmallBodies.terms: the API documentation (https://ssd-api.jpl.nasa.gov/doc/sb_ident.html, read 2026-10-24) carries no licence text; JPL small-body data are a NASA/JPL (United States Government) product. No licence was found, so the answers are not kept in the repository: this record keeps the URL pattern, the retrieval date, the SHA-256 of the three answers as retrieved (the file is gone) and the result of the search.
jplSmallBodies.alsoTried: IMCCE SkyBoT cone search (http://vo.imcce.fr/webservices/skybot/skybotconesearch_query.php and https://ssp.imcce.fr/webservices/skybot/api/conesearch.php): HTTP 403 and 502; nothing was retried or worked around.
